name: POST /api/leadflow/onboarding/:id/accept - acceptance is not completion
description:
CS takes the customer. ACCEPTANCE AND A BOOKED KICKOFF ARE SEPARATE FACTS (45f96ede-27d5-4c38-a4e1-a3e40df7fd56#AC2), and closed_won_terminal is their conjunction rather than a flag anybody sets. An accepted handoff with no meeting is somebody saying "yes, mine" and then nothing happening, which from the customer's side is identical to nobody accepting at all - and a single acceptance flag would let it count as done.

awaiting[] NAMES WHAT IS STILL OUTSTANDING, so the queue that shows an accepted-but-unbooked handoff says kickoff_booked rather than leaving somebody to work out why the record has not cleared.

CLOSED WON STAYS NON-TERMINAL until both land, which is what keeps the record in the pending list and inside the 24-hour alert. A record that goes quiet the moment payment clears is the failure SOP §50 names.

accepted_at uses COALESCE so a second acceptance does not overwrite the first - who took it and when is a fact about the past, and a re-accept is usually somebody adding the kickoff time they did not have the first time.

QA: accepts and books in one call, so the terminal branch is the one exercised; the handoff id is read from the cache.

testCases.name: Accepting with a booked kickoff makes Closed Won terminal
NEGATIVE: no handoff with that id
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: kickoff_at must be a valid date when supplied
errorCases.when: kickoff_at is present but does not parse. Accepting without a kickoff is legitimate and leaves Closed Won non-terminal; accepting with a date nobody can read is not.

errorCases.message: No onboarding handoff with that id
errorCases.when: the handoff id does not exist.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
